info.description:
This documentation provides details of all available ADvance API methods.

Please contact Abacus through your regular support channels should you require any further assistance.

Header values

The following header values are required to be supplied in all API method requests:

HTTP header namePurpose
ADAPI_ACCESS_HASHThis contains the access hash uniquely identifying the data domain area into which the request is made. Each ADvance brand entity uses a different ADAPI_ACCESS_HASH value.
ADAPI_ACCESS_TOKENThis is authorization token to perform the operation in question. This value is common for a single ADvance client/publisher.
ADAPI_RESPONSE_FORMATThis value determines the format of the response data. The default is xml. Possible values are 'xml' or 'json'.
### Response handling When handling any response from the ADvance API, **there must be consideration that additional XML/JSON elements may be added to the schema in future**. It should be noted that any existing elements in the response schema will not be modified in such changes to ensure compatibility with existing integrations.

Error handling

Handled error responses for API methods are structured as follows:

``` xml ERROR Invalid username/password. ```

Unhandled errors resulting from a generic unplanned technical error / exception in the method may result in an error code of 0 being returned. Such errors should be considered when integrating with the ADvance API methods.

``` xml ERROR ```

request.description:
This service is used to authenticate frontend users with AD based on the frontend cookie value. This cookie value is returned by the /Login method within the 'FrontendCookieValue' property element.

WVC/AD frontend sites set this value in a browser cookie named 'ADFEAuthCookie' at login. The WVC and AD frontends also look for this cookie if the user is not logged in, calling the /AutoLogin method and placing the user in a logged in state where validated. Where non-Abacus frontend sites are on the same main domain as the WVC/AD frontend sites, they may also set the 'ADFEAuthCookie' so that the login state is transferred between the sites.

Like the /Login method, this method will issue a UserToken for the AD party to be used in subsequent API requests.

request.description:
This service is used to retrieve party details in the same way as Regular user details method does (has the same output). The difference is that this method identifies the party in the system by its associated additional code representing the external system identifier of that party.

The type of this additional code is different for each client and is determined by publisher configuration setting “AdditionalCodeTypeForLegacyTranslation”.

After determining the Party ID the service will try to identify the user credentials for the brand associated to the token sent in HTTP header. As this is done using the “Passwordless login” method, this means that the user can have random credentials generated when option CONFIGURATION_TYPE_UID is 1 for the respective brand.
